title: The Windows shell self-test never completes: one destination captured, no report after 180 s
found: 2026-09-02, test-campaign phase 0, on the first run of this instrument since it was written
evidence: scripts/windows/run-shell-selftest.ps1 exits 2 `NOT-RUN: no selftest.json after 180 s`. shell-startup.log records two launches, 08:09:47.250 and 08:13:14.882, each followed by `loaded at rasterization scale 1.5` and nothing further. Exactly one capture is written, destination-discover.png at 103 KB - a real drawn board - and `discover` is the FIRST entry in DestinationCatalog.All. The process is gone afterwards: Get-Process MCPRouter.Shell returns nothing. Reproduced on a clean rebuild, scripts/windows/build-shell.ps1 exit 0.
mechanism: NOT ESTABLISHED, and deliberately not guessed. Two hypotheses were formed and both were killed by reading the code. (1) A blocking board constructor: SkillsBoard is the second destination and takes a live control client, but its constructor only wires `Loaded += OnLoaded` and issues no call. (2) An unhandled exception in that `async void` handler terminating the process: RefreshAsync catches only SkillsControlException, but LiveSkillsControlClient already catches HttpRequestException and TaskCanceledException and rethrows them typed. So the crash site is unknown and this defect is `inconclusive` on cause while being measured on effect.
why-it-matters: This is the only channel that can photograph the Windows boards - the agent session is Session 0, a WinUI process started there dies at 0xC000027B before App's constructor, and the interactive task's window station enumerates zero top-level windows so no external capture reaches it. Until this completes, per-destination pixel evidence exists for ONE of ten destinations and every raster claim about the other nine is inconclusive rather than failing.
contradicts: ORCHESTRATOR.md's WIN3 row records `self-test 0 (10/12/44)`. Either that run happened on a tree this one has diverged from, or on a machine state this one lacks - note control.token is absent here, which LiveSkillsControlClient's own documentation says means the router has never run on this machine.
next: Instrument SelfTestDriver to write its report incrementally and log each destination before it navigates, so the next run names the destination it dies on instead of leaving the question open.  ANSWERED 2026-09-02 by the out-of-process lane, which needed no instrumentation of the app at all: the destination it dies on is `skills`, the second in DestinationCatalog.All. See DEF-077. This defect remains open for the reporting half - the self-test still writes no selftest.json - but its `mechanism: NOT ESTABLISHED` is now narrowed to whatever DEF-077 finds.
resolution: FIXED 2026-09-02, and not by touching the self-test at all. Its cause was DEF-077: the driver walks DestinationCatalog.All in order, `discover` is first and `skills` is second, and Skills terminated the process - so the run died at board two, having written one capture and no report. With the SkillsBoard fragment namespace corrected, scripts/windows/run-shell-selftest.ps1 now exits 0 reporting `destinations walked: 10, appearances forced: 2, captures on disk: 12, no failures reported`, and the twelve PNGs are on disk. The `mechanism: NOT ESTABLISHED` this defect carried is answered: there was never a fault in the self-test.

title: WIN22's Action Center toasts cannot fire: nothing in product source raises a notification
found: 2026-09-02, tailings audit of the WIN fleet
evidence: `ToastNotificationManager` has 0 hits in product source. `AppNotification` has 0 - all 26 raw hits are under obj/ and bin/, generated Windows App SDK projection code. The only real `ToastNotification` hits are WIN22's own two files, where it is the type name of a plain record. The item ships NotificationModels.cs (17 lines), NotificationPresentation.cs (22) and a unit test (23), with no XAML and no view.
why-it-matters: The merge subject reads `WIN22: Windows toast notifications for waiting decisions - review-only actions, safe payloads, 621 tests` and the ledger row reads `Merged after verify PASS: 621 tests green, Action Center toast notifications`. The tests pass because they assert that a function building a payload record builds that payload record. No toast can reach the Action Center.
next: Either build the notification path - AppNotificationManager registration, an AppUserModelID, and the COM activator that makes a toast action reach the review sheet - or withdraw the claim from the ledger and the design of record.

title: WIN19's packaging and distribution ships no package: no manifest of any kind exists
found: 2026-09-02, tailings audit of the WIN fleet
evidence: A repository-wide search for `*.appxmanifest`, `Package.appxmanifest`, any winget manifest and any `*.wxs` returns nothing. The only winget/MSIX strings anywhere are WIN19's own PackagingModels.cs, PackagingPresentation.cs and their test - and their copies inside .worktrees/. The item is 3 source files totalling 67 added lines, with no XAML and no view.
why-it-matters: The ledger row reads `Merged after verify PASS: 608 tests green, winget and MSIX distribution channel contract, SmartScreen disclosure, clean uninstall rules`. There is no channel, no package and nothing to uninstall. A user cannot install this application by any of the means the item claims to have delivered.
next: Build the MSIX packaging project and the winget manifest, or reclassify the item as a distribution DESIGN and say so in the ledger.

title: WIN23's logon-task supervision registers no task: the model describes a mechanism nothing performs
found: 2026-09-02, tailings audit of the WIN fleet
evidence: `TaskService`, `schtasks`, `ServiceBase` and `StartupTask` appear in exactly two files, scripts/windows/run-shell-selftest.ps1 and scripts/windows/uia/run-probe-lane.ps1 - both WIN18/WIN20 harness scripts, neither WIN23's. LifecyclePresentation.cs maps DaemonSupervisionKind.LogonTask to the string `Scheduled Task at user logon (restarts on crash, un-elevated)`. Its test asserts that this function returns that string.
why-it-matters: The ledger row reads `Merged after verify PASS: 625 tests green, interactive user-session lifecycle model, logon task supervision, live reload contract`. Nothing supervises the router on Windows. The assertion behind the claim cannot fail for any reason connected to whether supervision works, which is the shape `warrant`'s cannot-fail scan exists to catch.
next: Either implement the registration - and a case at the effect-witness rung whose recorder is the Windows task scheduler itself - or record the item as a supervision MODEL awaiting an implementer.

title: The Discover detail dialog is unaddressable from the automation plane: no control carries a name
evidence: DiscoverDetailContent.xaml declares no literal Content on any control and no AutomationProperties.Name at all - it is one of only two view files in MCPRouter.Shell/Views with neither (the other is BoardPlaceholder.xaml, which is a placeholder by design).
why-it-matters: UI Automation is the only out-of-process channel this lane has. A surface whose controls carry no name cannot be asserted against by name, so every case on it would stand at `presence` at best. The same tree serves Narrator, so this is an accessibility defect and a measurability defect in one, exactly as WIN20's brief predicted.
next: Set AutomationProperties.Name on the dialog's controls, then register cases at the structural rung against them.

title: The Settings board declares one addressable control against a claim of seven sections of toggles
evidence: SettingsBoard.xaml yields exactly one literal control name, `Copy`, under a scan for Button/ToggleSwitch/CheckBox/ComboBox Content plus AutomationProperties.Name. The WIN13 ledger row claims `7 settings sections, Fluent ToggleSwitch controls`. MEASURED 2026-09-02: planning/evidence/WIN-SHELL/run/uia-shell-settings.json, captured after the destination was actuated through the automation plane, so this is the board as a user sees it rather than as the markup declares it.
mechanism: SETTLED 2026-09-02 against the running board, and it is the harsher of the two readings. The UIA control view of the live Settings board holds 60 elements and NOT ONE ToggleSwitch or CheckBox: 19 Text, 10 ListItem (the navigation pane), 9 Pane, 8 Button of which Minimize/Restore/Close/Close Navigation are window chrome, leaving `Copy` as the board's only actuable control - exactly the one name the XAML scan found. The toggle rows exist as prose only: `Launch router daemon at sign-in` and its subtitle `Starts the background loopback service automatically.` are published as Text with nothing actuable beside them. So the original either/or resolves to: there are no toggle controls in the realised tree at all. Whether they are absent from the XAML or present in a form that publishes no control is the remaining question, and it is now a question about 7 sections rather than about naming.
next: Open SettingsBoard.xaml and count what it actually declares against the WIN13 claim of seven sections. If the toggles are there, give them AutomationProperties.Name and re-run the lane; if they are not, the ledger row is what needs correcting. The lane already carries the check: uia-shell-settings.json is regenerated every run.

title: Selecting the Skills destination terminates MCPRouter.Shell
found: 2026-09-02, the first run of scripts/windows/uia/shell-lane.ps1 against the real shell
evidence: Reproduced on four consecutive lane runs, each on a freshly launched process. The lane launches MCPRouter.Shell in the interactive session, actuates each pane item through SelectionItemPattern.Select() out of process, and reads the tree back. `discover` selects and renders 55 named elements with the window title 'Discover'. Selecting `skills` ends the process: the window title read comes back empty, the control-view dump holds zero elements, and Get-Process returns nothing for the pid. Windows records it: Application Error 1000, MCPRouter.Shell.exe, exception code 0xC000027B in CoreMessagingXP.dll, with a matching WER APPCRASH bucket. shell-startup.log's last line for the run is `loaded at rasterization scale 1.5` and nothing after it.
mechanism: PARTLY ESTABLISHED. 0xC000027B is STATUS_STOWED_EXCEPTION, the WinRT mechanism for an unhandled exception surfacing out of a XAML callback, which matches SkillsBoard's `private async void OnLoaded(...) => await RefreshAsync();` - an async void handler, where an escaping exception terminates the process rather than faulting a task anybody awaits. What is NOT established is which throw escapes. RefreshAsync catches only SkillsControlException around each await, and LiveSkillsControlClient does convert HttpRequestException, TaskCanceledException, 404, 401 and JsonException into that typed error - so the read path is well guarded and the escaping exception is more likely to come from Render(), which builds XAML fragments by string concatenation and loads them, than from the client. That is a direction to look, not a finding, and it is recorded as such.
why-it-matters: It is the second of ten destinations and it takes the whole application with it, so a user who clicks Skills loses the window. It also explains DEF-071 without replacing it: the in-process self-test captures exactly one board, `destination-discover.png`, and then never writes its report - because `discover` is first in DestinationCatalog.All and `skills` is second, and the process does not survive the second. Two instruments, one in-process and one out-of-process, independently stop at the same boundary.
next: Give OnLoaded a try/catch that renders the failed state instead of terminating, which is the product fix; then find the escaping exception with a first-chance handler or by bisecting Render(). The lane's crash row is the regression test and it is already wired: this defect closes when `skills` reports pass rather than CRASH in planning/evidence/WIN-SHELL/run/assert-report.json.
resolution: FIXED 2026-09-02. Root cause named by the stack the new logging produced: SkillsBoard splices `FragmentNs` into 33 XAML fragments and FragmentNs declared ONLY the default namespace, while the fragments use `x:Name` - so `x:` was an undeclared prefix and XamlReader.Load threw. The first fragment to load is ErrorState's, which is what a board renders when no router is running, so it threw inside `async void OnLoaded` and took the process with it. Two changes: FragmentNs now declares xmlns:x, and OnLoaded catches rather than letting anything escape an async void. VERIFIED: `skills` reports pass on the lane, 57 elements, on a process that survives the whole ten-destination sweep with no relaunch.

title: Three destinations select in the pane and never open their board: Harnesses, Cleanup, Inbox
found: 2026-09-02, scripts/windows/uia/shell-lane.ps1 driving the real shell through UI Automation
evidence: Selecting Harnesses, Cleanup or Inbox through SelectionItemPattern.Select() leaves the window title, the caption band and the ENTIRE control-view tree byte-identical to the destination before it - the lane's fingerprint over the tree's accessible names is unchanged, which is why it is recorded as a COLLAPSE rather than as an empty board. The pane item itself does take the selection: SelectionItemPattern.Current.IsSelected reads True on all three. So the highlight moves and nothing behind it does. Order-independent: a reverse sweep, where every destination has a different predecessor, fails on exactly the same three. Six others - Discover, Servers, Activity, Checks, Insights, Settings - pass in both directions, so the harness, the actuation and the oracle all work.
mechanism: NARROWED, NOT ESTABLISHED. ShowDestination assigns `BoardHost.Content = destinationId switch {...}` and only THEN sets BoardTitle.Text and Title. An exception thrown while constructing the board abandons that statement and leaves all three unchanged, which is exactly the observed signature. The three failing boards are also the only three in the tree whose constructors do work beyond InitializeComponent: HarnessesBoard, CleanupBoard and InboxBoard each call `_model.PopulateSampleData()` and then a Render method, while every passing board either does nothing more or defers to a Loaded handler. That is a strong correlate and it is not proof, so no statement is named here. The app's own diagnostic cannot settle it - see DEF-079.
why-it-matters: This is the inert-shell shape the campaign exists to catch, and it survived every check the fleet ran: the boards compile, the pane draws all ten items with correct names, navigation was reviewed as honest by reading ShowDestination's switch (which is correct - all ten map to distinct board types), and the unit tests cover the models rather than the mounting. Three of nine boards - a third of the product's surface - cannot be opened by a user, and nothing in the repository said so until a harness actuated a control and read a state outside it.
next: Wrap the board construction in ShowDestination so a failing board renders a visible error state instead of silently leaving the previous one up - the silent failure is worse than the crash because it looks like a working application. Then construct HarnessesBoard, CleanupBoard and InboxBoard under a debugger or a first-chance handler to name the throw. This defect closes when all three report pass in planning/evidence/WIN-SHELL/run/assert-report.json.
resolution: FIXED 2026-09-02, and the mechanism that was NARROWED, NOT ESTABLISHED is now established - it was the constructor throw, as the correlate suggested, but the throw itself was one shared cause across all three: `SubtleButtonStyle` is not a WinUI 3 resource key and was never defined by this app. Eleven references across five views asked for it. Cleanup and Inbox threw inside InitializeComponent, Harnesses threw in its card builder, and the XAML ones surfaced as `XamlParseException: undeclared prefix`, which names neither the key nor the file. The style is now defined in App.xaml, based on the platform's DefaultButtonStyle. ShowDestination also now catches a failing board and mounts a visible BoardFailure card, so this class of fault can never again leave a working-looking application on screen. VERIFIED: all three report pass with real trees - Harnesses 70, Cleanup 90, Inbox 79 elements - and a mutation run that renames the style key turns exactly those three red again, which proves the lane's new failure-card check rather than its title check is what catches them. NOTE: AmbientFlyoutView and CapabilityDocumentPanel carry the same eleven-reference fault and are fixed by the same definition; neither has been opened by any harness, so both are fixed-but-unverified.

title: The shell's unhandled-exception log never fires, including for a crash that definitely had one
found: 2026-09-02, while trying to use it to diagnose DEF-077 and DEF-078
evidence:
App.xaml.cs registers `UnhandledException += (_, e) => StartupLog.Write($"unhandled: {e.Message}
{e.Exception}")`, whose comment says it is "the only trace a session that cannot see the desktop will ever have". shell-startup.log holds 16 launches across 2026-09-02 and not one `unhandled:` line - including the eight runs in which selecting Skills terminated the process with exception code 0xC000027B, which is by definition an unhandled exception. Every launch logs `launched` and `loaded at rasterization scale 1.5` and nothing else, so the log itself is being written.
mechanism: NOT ESTABLISHED. 0xC000027B is STATUS_STOWED_EXCEPTION raised in CoreMessagingXP.dll, and a stowed exception surfacing below the managed dispatch boundary may terminate the process without the Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Application.UnhandledException event ever being raised. That would make the handler correct and simply unreachable for this class of failure, which is a different remedy from a broken handler.
why-it-matters: It is the only diagnostic an agent session has for a GUI it cannot see, and its silence reads as `no exception occurred` when it means `nothing was recorded`. That inversion cost real time on DEF-077 and DEF-078: the absence of a log line had to be discounted as evidence before either could be reasoned about honestly.
next: Add AppDomain.CurrentDomain.UnhandledException and TaskScheduler.UnobservedTaskException beside the XAML handler, and have SkillsBoard's async void OnLoaded log-and-render rather than let an exception escape. Then re-run the lane and require an `unhandled:` line for the Skills crash before this closes - an empty log must stop being indistinguishable from a clean run.
resolution: PARTLY ADDRESSED 2026-09-02. AppDomain.CurrentDomain.UnhandledException and TaskScheduler.UnobservedTaskException are now registered beside the XAML handler, and ShowDestination and SkillsBoard.OnLoaded both log their own failures - which is what produced the stack traces that resolved DEF-077 and DEF-078 within one run of adding them. STAYS OPEN because the two new handlers have not been observed firing: every exception since has been caught at a site that logs it directly, so nothing has reached them. An unproven handler is exactly the thing this defect is about, and closing it on the strength of registration would repeat the error it records.
